title: Dynamic-label sentinel in MATCH defers to a Filter, not a plan-time catalog lookup
description: `MATCH (n:$label)` stores `$label` verbatim as a sentinel string in the node pattern's `labels` list. The planner (`QueryPlanner`) has no access to query parameters — those live only on the execution context, constructed after planning. Calling `self.catalog.get_or_create_label("$label")` at plan time resolves (and even creates) a literal label named `$label` instead of the runtime value, so the scan silently returns zero rows — a silent-wrong-results bug, not a crash. The fix mirrors how `WHERE n:$x` already worked: defer resolution to execution. When the FIRST label of a node pattern starts with `$`, the planner must not call `get_or_create_label` on it; instead emit `AllNodesScan` + `Filter("{variable}:{first_label}")`, the same lowering already used for the second-and-later labels in a multi-label pattern. The Filter operator already resolves a `$`-prefixed label against `context.params` at execution time: a non-empty STRING becomes the label, anything else (missing/NULL/empty/non-STRING) collapses to no rows, never an error.
whenToUse: Any time a planner needs to resolve a `$param`-sentinel value only available on the execution context (labels, relationship types, property keys referenced dynamically) and the executor already has a working runtime resolution path for the same sentinel in a different clause. Reuse that existing runtime resolution instead of inventing a second resolution mechanism at plan time.
whenNotToUse: Do not resolve a `$`-prefixed sentinel via any catalog get-or-create call at plan time — it treats the literal sentinel string as a real name and pollutes the catalog with a spurious literal label/type, silently producing empty results instead of an error. If no downstream operator already has runtime `$param` resolution for the entity kind in question, build that resolution first — don't half-apply this pattern by routing to a Filter that doesn't understand the sentinel.
